normal_conventions: All nine theorem-like environments (thm, lem, coro, prop, exemple, rem, defn, notation, fait) share the single counter declared at L23–33, so printed numbers 1–50 run through one sequence; prop 3.18 (370–376) and prop 4.11 (554–556) therefore carry no label and downstream references must use line spans.
The appendix is plain \appendix plus \section*; the three proof environments at 568–608, 612–636 and 638–656 belong to body results (Corollaire 3.9, fait 4.9, lem 4.9), not to new appendix results.
lem fubini (600–605) is nested inside the appendix proof of Corollaire 3.9 and still consumes a printed number, which belongs to the appendix range rather than to Section 4.

The paper contains no figure, tabular, tikzpicture or includegraphics in the 661 native lines; the only raster images in the reader are the cover (P1) and the title/catalog page (P2), so no unit needs figure assets.

ORIGINAL_HEADING_ALIGNMENT.json and ORIGINAL_READER_ANCHORS.json attach the single label 'fubini' to all 50 positions; that field is a shared-label artefact and is not used as per-position label evidence here. Per-position labels were re-extracted from the native lines.
Statement spans of the two units never overlap (288–292 / 330–335 / 354–357 / 370–376 vs 474–477 / 487–496 / 530–537 / 554–556), and their proof spans share no line.
scope: C1 quantifies over ξ in 𝒢 (all α^⊥ removed) and over diophantine (p,q); it does not claim the property for every period, and L222 states the missing modulus is only known generic.
C2's density is 'pour presque tout ξ' with r arbitrary; 𝒜(ξ) is only guaranteed non-empty on the full-measure set A, so no pointwise statement is available.

Zero/full measure is always relative to the Lebesgue measure class on the smooth period domain (rem 22, 293–295); the lattice property of Γ is cited from Borel–Harish-Chandra, not proved (notation 23, 298–300).
C1 and C2 are separate cores: C2 uses prop 3.16 as a deducted input, C1 uses nothing from Section 4. Statements and proofs of the two units occupy no common line.
